pointers.sentence: One table holds the rows of every model, whose keys may be integers, strings or UUIDs; `object_id` is a `TextField`, "the textual representation" of the key in the documentation (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).
The migration `0002` replaced `action_time`'s `auto_now=True` with that default; `0003` gave `action_flag` its choices (`django/contrib/admin/migrations/`).

One entry is saved with `Model.save`, several together by `QuerySet.bulk_create` ([`bulk_create` and `bulk_update`](../querysets/bulk.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntryManager.log_actions`).

The three methods of `ModelAdmin` are the hooks: each calls `log_actions` with the request's user and its flag, and a project overrides them to log elsewhere or not at all (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.log_addition`).

Called after it, `log_actions`, which iterates what it is given, would find a queryset empty once `ModelAdmin.delete_queryset` had run, and instances whose keys the collector had set to `None` (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.delete`).

`ModelAdmin.construct_change_message` hands the form, the formsets and whether the object is new to `django.contrib.admin.utils.construct_change_message`, which returns a list: `{"added": {}}` for an addition, or else `{"changed": {"fields": [...]}}` with the labels of the fields that changed, if any; then an `"added"`, `"changed"` or `"deleted"` entry for each object a formset added, changed or deleted, with the model's verbose name and the object's text (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:construct_change_message`).
Anything else, a deletion's empty string or a sentence a project wrote, is returned as it is (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntry.get_change_message`).

`LogEntry.get_admin_url` reverses `"admin:fleet_ship_change"`, or its like, with the key quoted, and gives `None` without a content type, a key or such a URL; it does not ask whether the object exists, and gave /admin/fleet/ship/2/change/ for Beagle's deletion (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntry.get_admin_url`).

`ModelAdmin.history_view` loads the object with `ModelAdmin.get_object`, asks `BaseModelAdmin.has_view_or_change_permission`, and raises `PermissionDenied` before it looks whether there was an object; only then is a missing object sent to the index with a warning (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.history_view`). nora got 403 for voyage 99's history, and a redirect for ship 99's.
The history view answers 403 to staff without the view or change permission whether the object exists or not (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

`AdminSite.each_context` gives every page `"log_entries"`, the queryset of `AdminSite.get_log_entries`: every row, its content type and user joined, not yet evaluated (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_log_entries`).

Of the admin's templates only the index evaluates it, with `{% get_admin_log 10 as admin_log for_user user %}`, whose node keeps one user's rows and takes the newest ten (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/log.py:AdminLogNode.render`); nora's change list sent no query of the log.

Each entry links to `LogEntry.get_admin_url` unless it is a deletion or has none, under its content type's name or "Unknown content" (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/index.html`). piet's listed the change of nora, Beagle's deletion without a link, and Genoa's addition.
